title: Micro-batch hypothesis log — morning run
content:
> Quick capture of morning micro-batching experiments, triage items, and kernel notes.

Goals for today:
- Narrow candidate micro-batch sizes for small-seq (<128) and long-seq (1024+) paths.
- Reproduce the 15% p99 spike observed on canary at 03/11 22:14 UTC.
- Sketch potential KV eviction heuristic tweaks to avoid cold-KV stalls.

Observations (from canary logs / local repro):
- Baseline canary (model: r-infer-13B-q8) saw p50=38ms, p95=210ms, p99=480ms over 10k requests (mixed seq).
- The spike cluster correlates with a cohort of requests that have a long prefix + sudden short continuation (~90% cache miss rate).
- Throughput didn't drop, but tail latency doubled for those cohorts.

Quick repro steps I ran locally (commands):
- ./bench --model r-infer-13B-q8 --seq 64 --batch 1 --requests 2000 --seed 42
- ./bench --model r-infer-13B-q8 --seq 1024 --batch 8 --requests 1000 --workload-mix config/mix-longprefix.json
- sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- ./server --port 9001 (grabbed flame for stalled kernel ops)

Key hypotheses:
1) Micro-batching boundary crossing: when the runtime switches from continuous-batching to queued micro-batches we see serialization overhead + extra kernel memory touches that lengthen KV lookup latency.
   - Repro: synthetic stream with alternating small/large seq lengths causes pattern.
2) Eviction thrash combined with GC work: large prefixes cause huge KV entries; eviction flips pages leading to page faults for currently-serving requests.
   - Evidence: perf shows increased major page faults during spike window.
3) Lock contention on KV-cache metadata when many small updates happen concurrently (rare, but high-cost).

Quick notes from kernel traces:
- top stacks:
  - runtime::kv::lookup -> runtime::kv::maybe_refresh -> kmalloc
  - runtime::batch::flush -> uv_poll -> epoll_wait (timing shows micro-sleeps)
- observed heavy spend in memcpy near the end of sequences (possible suboptimal memcopies for compressed kv items).

Experiment plan (ordered, quick-to-run):
A) Narrow micro-batch sizes (fast, local)
   1) Run 1..8, 9..16, 17..32 fixed micro-batch settings against mix file. Log p50/p95/p99 and kernel faults.
   2) Add instrumentation: count cache-miss vs cache-hit per request, dump KV sizes distribution.
B) Controlled eviction tests (mid complexity)
   1) Pin a long-prefix heavy synthetic workload and toggle eviction policies: LRU(100MB), size-aware-LRU, time-decay.
   2) Measure tail per-policy and page fault counts.
C) Lock contention microbench (longer)
   1) Stress KV metadata updates with 200 concurrent small requests; check futex waits in perf.

To-do (my immediate):
- [ ] Run A1 with seeds [7,42,99] and push results to PR notes. (priority: high)
- [ ] Add small KV-hist dump to /metrics/export for per-request KV-count. (priority: medium)
- [ ] Create JIRA RT tickets for eviction policy tuning and micro-batch boundary fix: JIRA-RT-918 (eviction), JIRA-RT-919 (batch switch). (priority: high)
- [ ] Ask SRE if canary nodes had kernel updates around 03/10-03/11 (Slack to #sre-runtime). (priority: low)

Triage list (short):
- JIRA-RT-917: "p99 spike on canary during mixed seq" — owner: Diego (assigned). Notes: Diego confirmed local repro with mix file.
- GIT #482: PR adds micro-batch timeout heuristic. Needs more perf data before merge.

Notes for follow-up conversation with Priya (PM)
- If micro-batching boundary is real, optimal knob might be an adaptive threshold based on recent seq length percentiles rather than static sizes.
- For Dedicated customers with strict latency SLOs, consider offering an opt-in no-eviction mode if they pay for reserved capacity.

Rough data snapshot (local run A1, 2026-03-12 09:14):
- micro-batch=8, seq-mix (20% long, 80% short) --> p50=42ms, p95=230ms, p99=490ms
- micro-batch=4, same mix --> p50=39ms, p95=195ms, p99=300ms
- page_faults: 420 (mb=8) vs 120 (mb=4) over 10k requests

Ideas to try (brain dump):
- lightweight prefix-caching: keep hot small prefixes in a tiny inline cache to avoid big-kv walks.
- quantify benefit of zero-copy for KV items (reduce memcpy).
- experiment: avoid eviction during a request's lifetime (pin-on-lookup for X ms).

Questions / unknowns:
- Why is mb=8 worse than mb=4 for p99 on same throughput? (suspect boundary + page thrash)
- Is there a user workload pattern (prefix-heavy) hitting the canary? Need sample traces (anonymized).

Meeting notes to paste later:
- 11:00 sync with Diego + Priya; bring initial A1 results, perf flame, and hypothesis list.

End of capture.

-- Morgan
